text: Việt Nam becomes Singapore's second-largest seafood supplier by volume
HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam has become Singapore's second-largest seafood supplier by volume, ranking just behind Malaysia.
The country shipped 21,085 tonnes of seafood to Singapore in the first nine months of this year, up 7.6 per cent year-on-year.
Strong performances across key product categories, particularly pangasius, squid and surimi, have further strengthened Việt Nam's market position.

According to Enterprise Singapore data cited by the Việt Nam Trade Office in Singapore, Singapore's seafood imports (HS Code 03) reached SGD923.2 million in January-September this year, up 6.1 per cent year on year.
Imports from Việt Nam grew faster, rising by 7.7 per cent to SGD95.4 million and lifting its market share from 10.2 per cent to 10.3 per cent.
Việt Nam also overtook Japan to rank fourth among Singapore's seafood suppliers by value, following a 10.3 per cent increase in shipments to SGD34.6 million in the third quarter.
Malaysia led with SGD129.8 million, followed by Indonesia at SGD106.3 million and China at SGD96.7 million.
Competitive pricing remains a major advantage.
Việt Nam's average export price stood at SGD4,525 per tonne, approximately 54 per cent of the market average.
Export growth was largely volume-driven, with higher shipment volumes contributing around SGD6.4 million of the SGD6.8 million increase in export value.

Fish fillets and fresh, chilled or frozen fish meat remained Việt Nam's largest seafood export category to Singapore, generating nearly SGD50 million, up 10 per cent, and accounting for 52.4 per cent of total imports from Việt Nam.
Frozen pangasius fillets alone reached SGD34.9 million, with Việt Nam commanding a dominant 95.4 per cent market share.
Other products also recorded significant growth.
Dried anchovies increased by 28.3 per cent, dried cuttlefish and squid surged by 63.7 per cent, while surimi exports rose by 59.3 per cent in value.
Frozen black tiger shrimp exports climbed by 60.2 per cent, while whiteleg shrimp shipments increased 4.7-fold.
Looking ahead, demand is expected to remain stable towards the end of this year and ahead of the upcoming Lunar New Year, creating opportunities for Vietnamese exporters.

However, intensifying competition from Ecuador, India and Indonesia, alongside stricter food safety and traceability requirements expected to be fully implemented from 2028, will require businesses to upgrade their capabilities.

The Việt Nam Trade Office advises exporters to move beyond price-based competition by investing in deeper processing, higher-value products, product diversification and brand development to secure sustainable growth in Singapore. - VNS
